definition_zh: 记号；痕迹；标记；符号；分数；留下痕迹；注意
definition_en: a small visible trace or spot; a written sign or symbol; a grade given for schoolwork; to leave a visible trace; to notice or pay attention to

sceneCN: 这里指留在纸面上的可见痕迹（第 1 个义项：记号、痕迹）；句意为海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

senses.title: A visible spot or line left on a surface
senses.definition: a small area of damage, colour or dirt that shows something has touched or pressed a surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面上一小块颜色、污迹或破损，显示有东西接触或压过
senses.example: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。
senses.why: Old English mearc first named a boundary sign, a visible thing set down to show where something is or has happened, and that visible trace is the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mearc 最初指边界的标志，是一件看得见的东西，用来说明某物在哪里或发生过什么；这种可见的痕迹就是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A written sign or symbol
senses.definition: a sign, symbol or written figure used to represent something or to give information
senses.definitionCN: 用来代表某物或提供信息的符号、记号或书写图样
senses.example: Put a mark beside the name of the candidate you prefer.
senses.exampleCN: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。
senses.why: Once a visible sign can stand for something other than itself, the boundary trace becomes a symbol, and writing turns that symbol into a small reusable unit of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当一件可见的标记能够代表它自身以外的东西，边界痕迹就变成符号，而文字又把这个符号变成可反复使用的小单位。

senses.title: A score or grade given for work
senses.definition: a number or letter showing how well a piece of schoolwork or a performance has been judged
senses.definitionCN: 表示某份作业或某次表现被评为多好的数字或字母
senses.example: She was pleased with the mark she received on the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的作文分数很满意。
senses.why: A teacher's mark was once a physical sign placed next to an answer; because that sign recorded quality, the sign itself came to mean the judgement written into it.
senses.whyCN: 教师的 mark 原是画在答案旁边的一个实记号；正因为这个记号记录了优劣，记号本身便转而表示写在里面的评判。

senses.title: To leave a visible trace on something
senses.definition: to make a visible spot, line or sign on a surface, often to identify or record something
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上留下可见的点、线或符号，常用来识别或记录
senses.example: She marked the page with a folded corner before returning the book.
senses.exampleCN: 她折了个角给那一页做记号，然后才把书还回去。
senses.why: The verb is the noun put into action: to mark is to produce the very trace that the noun names, and the purpose is usually to make something findable later.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词化为动作：mark 某物，就是造出名词所指的那种痕迹，目的通常是让某样东西日后能被找到。

senses.title: To notice or pay attention to
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, especially because it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，尤因它值得被记住
senses.example: Mark my words: the second attempt will be harder than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 记住我的话：第二次尝试会比第一次更难。
senses.why: A mark draws the eye to one spot, so to mark something in speech is to single it out mentally and ask the listener to keep it in view.
senses.whyCN: 记号把目光引向某一处，所以在言语中说 mark 某事，就是在心里把它单独标出，并要求听者一直记着。

intro.en: Mark began as a Germanic word for a boundary sign, and from that visible sign it grew into a trace, a symbol, a grade and an act of attention.
intro.cn: mark 起初是日耳曼语中表示边界标志的词，从那个可见的标志出发，长出痕迹、符号、分数与注意等义。

items.en: The boundary sense is usually traced to a reconstructed root *merg-, meaning a border or edge, though the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 边界义一般认为可追溯到重构词根 *merg-，意为边界、边缘，但这一重构并不完全确定。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *markō meant a boundary and a sign set on it, and it is the base of the English word.
items.cn: 重构名词 *markō 意为边界以及立在边界上的标志，是英语这个词的词基。

items.en: Old English mearc covered a boundary, a landmark and a sign, so the word already joined the idea of an edge to the idea of something visible.
items.cn: 古英语 mearc 同时表示边界、地标和标志，这个词已经把「边缘」与「看得见的东西」连在一起。

items.en: Middle English mark widened to any trace, target or written symbol, and school use added the sense of a judgement written beside an answer.
items.cn: 中古英语 mark 扩展到任何痕迹、目标或书写符号，学校里的用法又增加了「写在答案旁边的评判」这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb of noticing and the compounds marker, bookmark and trademark, while the border sense survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示「注意」的动词，以及 marker、bookmark、trademark 等复合词，边界义则主要留存在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on mark and its old boundary root; the near-meaning group gathers words for signs, stains and grades.
note.cn: 形近组收由 mark 及其古老边界词根构成的形式；近义组收表示符号、污迹与分数的词。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a boundary sign cut into the ground, becomes any visible trace, and then any symbol, judgement or act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从刻在地面上的边界标志开始，先变成任何可见的痕迹，再变成符号、评判或注意的动作。

normal.en: Old English mearc meant a boundary and a sign, so the word began with something placed on the ground to show where one thing ends and another begins.
normal.cn: 古英语 mearc 意为边界与标志，所以这个词起初指放在地面上的东西，用来说明一物到何处为止、另一物从何处开始。

normal.en: The same old sense survives in the Welsh marches, a border region, and in the Latin relative margo, a margin or edge.
normal.cn: 同样的旧义留存在威尔士边境这一地名里，也留存在拉丁语近亲 margo（页边、边缘）中。

normal.en: A school mark began as a sign written beside an answer, and the sign came to stand for the judgement it recorded.
normal.cn: 学校的 mark 原是写在答案旁的记号，后来这个记号转而代表它所记录的评判。

normal.en: The verb mark is the noun turned into an action: the trace and the act of making it share one form.
normal.cn: 动词 mark 是名词化为动作：痕迹与留下痕迹的行为共用一种形式。

normal.en: Mark my words uses the physical sign as a mental one: the words are singled out so the listener will not forget them.
normal.cn: Mark my words 把实体的记号用作心里的记号：把话单独标出，让听者不会忘记。

abstract.en: A single red circle can point to a reef, a name or a mistake, because a mark is attention made visible.
abstract.cn: 一个小小的红圈可以指向礁石、名字或错误，因为记号就是被看见的注意。

abstract.en: A boundary and a symbol are the same gesture: something small is placed to say this is where meaning begins.
abstract.cn: 边界与符号是同一个动作：放下某件小小的东西，说「意义从这里开始」。

abstract.en: To mark a word in a book is to ask the page to remember for you.
abstract.cn: 在书里给一个词做记号，就是请纸页替你记住。

examples.en: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
examples.cn: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

examples.en: Put a mark beside the name of the candidate you prefer.

examples.en: She marked the page with a folded corner before returning the book.

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a visible trace placed on a surface; the written symbol, the grade, the act of marking and the mental act of noticing all grow from that one visible sign.

sensesIntro.cn: store 是商店、备好的储备，或储存的行为。

core.en: Goods held until someone needs them.
core.cn: 货物被存着，直到有人需要。

branches.en: The store opens at nine.
branches.cn: 这家店九点开门。

branches.en: They keep a store of wood.
branches.cn: 他们存着一批木柴。

branches.en: We stored the boxes in the attic.
branches.cn: 我们把箱子存在阁楼里。

branches.en: A shop is simply a store of goods on show.
branches.cn: 商店不过是将存货摆出来给人看。

branches.en: To store is to build a store for later.
branches.cn: 储存，就是为以后备下一份库存。

intro.en: Store takes endings and builds words for shops and keeping.
intro.cn: store 加词尾，构成与商店和存放相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source instaurare meant to set up or renew.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 instaurare 意为建立或更新。

items.exampleCN: 储存谷物需要干燥的空气。

items.meaning: a large shop with many sections
items.example: She works in a department store.
items.exampleCN: 她在一家百货商店工作。

latinEntries.structure: Latin instaurare to Old French estorer

definition_zh: 领带；绳子；联系；平局；系；绑；打结；打平
definition_en: to fasten something with string or rope, or a strip of cloth worn round the neck; also a bond between people or a level score
core_image: 两根绳头被拉紧打成一个结，两样东西从此连在一起
scene: 比赛进入最后一分钟，两队分数还完全相同。 The two teams were still tied at two goals each when the whistle blew.
sceneCN: 这里 tie 是「打成平局」（第 7 个义项：比分相同）；句意为哨响时两队仍是二比二平。画面里有记分牌、哨子与球员。

pos.zh: 动词：系、绑、打结；打平；相配
名词：领带；绳子；联系；平局

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「解开；松开」
由过去分词形容词化，义为「被系住的；捆绑的」
复合词，义为「决胜局；平局决胜」
由现在分词名词化，义为「打结；系缚的动作」

senses.title: To fasten with string or rope
senses.definition: to fasten something or someone with string, rope, or a similar material
senses.definitionCN: 用绳子或类似材料把某物或某人固定住
senses.example: He tied the boat to the post before the storm came.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，他把小船拴在柱子上。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to bind, and every later sense grows out of that single act of pulling two things together.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词意为「捆绑」，此后所有义项都从这一个把两样东西拉在一起的动作长出。

senses.title: To make a knot
senses.definition: to form a knot by crossing and pulling the ends of a string
senses.definitionCN: 把绳子的两端交叉拉紧做成结
senses.example: She tied her shoelaces twice to be safe.
senses.exampleCN: 为了保险，她把鞋带系了两道。
senses.why: A knot is what a bind leaves behind: a small permanent object made of the act of binding.
senses.whyCN: 结是捆绑留下的东西：一个由捆绑动作做成的小小固定物。

senses.title: A necktie
senses.definition: a narrow strip of cloth worn around the neck and tied at the front
senses.definitionCN: 系在颈前打结的窄条布料
senses.example: He chose a dark tie for the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑了一条深色领带参加面试。
senses.why: The tie is literally a binding round the neck, wearing the original act on the body.
senses.whyCN: 领带就是颈上的一圈系缚，把原始动作穿在了身上。

senses.title: A bond between people
senses.definition: a connection of affection, duty, or shared experience between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间由感情、责任或共同经历形成的连结
senses.example: The two sisters kept a close tie after moving to different cities.
senses.exampleCN: 搬去不同城市后，两姐妹仍保持紧密的联系。
senses.why: Two separate lives are bound together just as two ends are bound in a knot.
senses.whyCN: 两条独立的生活被绑在一起，正如两个绳头在结中相绑。

senses.title: A draw in a game
senses.definition: a result in which two sides have the same score
senses.definitionCN: 双方得分相同的结果
senses.example: The final ended in a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛以平局收场。
senses.why: No side is pulled tighter than the other, so the two remain bound level on the scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 两边谁都没被拉得更紧，于是在记分牌上停在同一水平。

senses.title: To score level
senses.definition: to make the score equal in a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或竞赛中把比分拉成相同
senses.example: A late goal tied the game at one each.
senses.exampleCN: 临近终场的一个进球把比分扳成一比一。
senses.why: The verb repeats the noun: the sides become bound level by a single action.
senses.whyCN: 动词复现了名词：一次动作让双方落到同一水平。

senses.title: To be tied at a score
senses.definition: to be in a position where both sides have the same score in a match
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中双方得分相同的状态
senses.example: The teams were tied at two goals each when the whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 哨响时两队仍是二比二平。
senses.why: A level score holds the two sides together, unable to break away.
senses.whyCN: 平分把双方拴在一起，谁也无法拉开。

senses.title: To be connected with
senses.definition: to be closely connected with or to match another thing
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物密切相关或相互配合
senses.example: The new album ties in with the film of the same name.
senses.exampleCN: 这张新专辑与同名电影相互配合。
senses.why: What is joined by a string moves together, so things that must be understood together are said to tie in.
senses.whyCN: 用绳连着的东西会一起移动，因此须一同理解的事物也说成 tie in。

senses.title: A railway sleeper
senses.definition: a heavy wooden or concrete support laid across a railway track
senses.definitionCN: 横铺在铁轨下的粗木或混凝土支撑物
senses.example: The workers replaced every tie along the old line.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们更换了旧线路上的每一根枕木。
senses.why: The sleeper is a tie because it ties the two steel rails to a fixed distance.
senses.whyCN: 枕木之所以叫 tie，是因为它把两条钢轨拴在固定间距上。

senses.title: To restrict by duty
senses.definition: to limit someone's freedom of action by duty, rules, or promises
senses.definitionCN: 通过责任、规则或承诺限制某人的行动自由
senses.example: The contract ties him to the company for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把他约束在公司三年。
senses.why: A bound person cannot move away, so obligation is described with the rope word.
senses.whyCN: 被绑住的人走不开，于是义务也用这条绳子的词来表达。

intro.en: The noun and verb both go back to Old English, where the sense of a cord or bond already covered fastening, and the sport sense of an equal score is much later.
intro.cn: 名词与动词都可追溯到古英语，当时「绳、束缚」的意思已包含捆绑之意，「比分相同」的体育义项出现很晚。

items.en: The noun teag and the verb tiegan meant a cord and to bind.
items.cn: 名词 teag 与动词 tiegan 意为「绳」和「捆绑」。

items.en: The verb covered not only ropes but any obligation that holds a person.
items.cn: 这个动词不仅指绳子，也指任何把人拴住的义务。

items.en: The word settles into the modern spelling tie and keeps both cord and bond.
items.cn: 这个词定型为现代拼写 tie，同时保留「绳索」与「纽带」两层。

items.en: The necktie sense becomes common in the nineteenth century with formal dress.
items.cn: 领带义项在十九世纪随正式着装普及。

items.en: Sports writing extends the word to an equal score and to scoring level.
items.cn: 体育报道把本词扩展到平分与追平比分。

items.en: Railway use names the sleeper that ties the rails to gauge.
items.cn: 铁路用语用本词命名把钢轨固定在轨距上的枕木。

note.en: The look-alikes share the spelling pattern of the short stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for binding and for drawn results.
note.cn: 形近组围绕这个短词干的拼写，近义组则收集其它表示捆绑与平局结果的词。

entries.definition: to undo a knot or a fastening
entries.definitionCN: 解开；松开

entries.definition: fastened with rope, or level in score
entries.definitionCN: 被系住的；打平的

entries.definition: the act of fastening with string
entries.definitionCN: 打结；系缚

entries.definition: one of several rows or levels, a different word in origin
entries.definitionCN: 一层；一排，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to tie something tightly together
entries.definitionCN: 捆绑；束紧

entries.definition: to attach or close something firmly
entries.definitionCN: 系牢；扣紧

entries.definition: a result with equal scores
entries.definitionCN: 平局

entries.definition: a join made by tying thread or rope
entries.definitionCN: 结；绳结

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the original meaning of binding, from common phrases, and from the word family.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「捆绑」的本义、常用短语与词族出发。

normal.en: Tie means to bind, so a business tie binds people just as a rope binds a boat.
normal.cn: tie 意为捆绑，所以生意上的 tie 像绳子系船一样把人绑在一起。

normal.en: Untie is un- plus tie, the prefix doing the work of loosening.
normal.cn: untie 是 un- 加 tie，前缀做的就是松开的活。

normal.en: Tie up means both to fasten and to occupy, because a tied thing cannot be used freely.
normal.cn: tie up 既指系紧也指占用，因为被绑住的东西不能自由使用。

normal.en: A tie in football ties the two scores to the same number.
normal.cn: 足球里的 tie 把两边的比分拴在同一个数上。

normal.en: The spelling change to tying keeps the y after a vowel, as in dying.
normal.cn: 变成 tying 时 y 保留在元音后，和 dying 一样。

abstract.en: Picture two loose ends pulled in opposite directions until the knot snaps tight.
abstract.cn: 想象两个松散的绳头被向反方向拉，直到结猛然收紧。

abstract.en: Think of a necktie as a rope that fashion has made polite.
abstract.cn: 把领带想成一条被时尚变得得体的绳子。

abstract.en: A draw on the scoreboard is a rope holding both teams at the same height.
abstract.cn: 记分牌上的平局就是一根把两队拉在同一高度的绳。

examples.en: He tied the parcel with brown string.
examples.cn: 他用棕色细绳把包裹捆好。

examples.en: The game ended in a tie, so both teams stayed on the field.
examples.cn: 比赛以平局结束，两队都留在了场上。

examples.en: Strong family ties helped her through the difficult year.
examples.cn: 牢固的家庭纽带帮她度过了艰难的一年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太」——绳子拉得太紧，一下就系上了。

root: 古英语 teag（绳、带）与 tiegan（捆绑）同源，属日耳曼语族固有词，与德语 Zick 无直接关系；「领带」义十九世纪成形，「平局」义来自体育报道的引申。

sensesIntro.en: From the single act of binding grow the cord, the necktie, the bond between people, the level score, and the duty that limits freedom, while the railway sleeper keeps the most literal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「捆绑」这一个动作长出绳索、领带、人际纽带、平分比分与限制自由的责任，而铁路枕木保留了最字面的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two ends pulled together and held by a knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个绳头被拉到一起，被一个结固定住。

branches.en: The physical act and its result.
branches.cn: 物理动作及其结果。

branches.en: Objects made of a binding.
branches.cn: 由系缚做成的东西。

branches.en: Binding carried into human relationships.
branches.cn: 系缚进入人际关系。

branches.en: Binding two scores level.
branches.cn: 把两个比分拴成同一水平。

branches.en: Things joined in meaning or held by duty.
branches.cn: 意义上相连或由义务拴住的事物。

intro.en: The word is native, so the affix work here is about the un- prefix and the spelling of its inflections rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 本词是本土词，因此这里讲的是 un- 前缀与其屈折拼写，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin original lies behind tie; the Latin items are listed only for comparison with borrowed words of similar meaning.
latinIntro.cn: tie 背后没有拉丁原词；所列拉丁词仅与近义借词作对照。

items.meaningCN: 表示「捆绑」的古英语词干
items.example: The whole word is this stem with no added ending.
items.exampleCN: 整词就是这个词干，未加任何后缀。
untie 把系上的动作反过来。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词结尾
items.example: Tied also serves as an adjective.
Tying keeps a y before the ending.
items.exampleCN: tying 在词尾前保留 y。

items.example: Ties serves as plural and third person.
items.exampleCN: ties 既是复数也是第三人称单数。

items.meaning: used at the start of compounds
items.example: Tie-break names a game that settles a draw.
items.exampleCN: tie-break 指结束平局的决胜局。

items.example: A tie-clip holds a tie to a shirt.
items.exampleCN: tie-clip 把领带夹在衬衫上。

items.example: A tie-less shirt needs no necktie.
items.exampleCN: tie-less 形容不戴领带的衬衫。

definition_zh: 记得；想起；记住去做；代问好；纪念
definition_en: to keep something in your mind or bring it back into your mind
core_image: 多年后仍能准确说出那天的天气和气味
scene: 多年以后，她还能说出那家小店门口挂着什么颜色的帘子。 Years later, she could still remember the colour of the curtain at the shop door.
sceneCN: 这里 remember 是「记得」（第 1 个义项：把过去的经历保存在心里并能想起）；句意：多年以后，她仍然记得那家店门口帘子的颜色。

derivatives.zh: remember 加 -ance 构成，义为「记忆；纪念」
与 remember 共享拉丁词根 memor，义为「记忆」
由 memor 加 -able 构成，义为「难忘的」

senses.title: To keep something in mind
senses.definition: to have a fact, a name, or an experience stored in your mind and be able to bring it back
senses.definitionCN: 把事实、名字或经历存在心里，并能重新想起来
senses.example: I remember my first day at school very clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 我清楚地记得上学的第一天。
senses.why: The Latin verb rememorari means to be mindful again, so the core image is a stored scene coming back whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rememorari 意为「重新留心」，所以核心画面是储存的场景被完整唤回。

senses.title: To not forget to do something
senses.definition: to keep a future task in mind so that you do not fail to do it
senses.definitionCN: 把将来的任务放在心里，以免忘记去做
senses.example: Remember to lock the door when you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开时记得锁门。
senses.why: The stored scene here points forward: keeping a duty in mind until the moment arrives.
senses.whyCN: 这里的记忆指向前方：把职责放在心里，直到该行动的时刻。

senses.title: To send greetings through someone
senses.definition: to ask someone to pass your greetings to another person
senses.definitionCN: 请某人把自己的问候带给另一个人
senses.example: Please remember me to your parents.
senses.exampleCN: 请代我向你父母问好。
senses.why: Holding a person in mind turns into a spoken greeting sent through a third party.
senses.whyCN: 把某人放在心上，就变成托第三个人带去的问候。

senses.title: To honour the memory of someone
senses.definition: to keep the memory of a person or event alive with respect
senses.definitionCN: 怀着敬意让某个人或某件事的记忆继续存在
senses.example: The town holds a service to remember the victims.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上举行仪式纪念遇难者。
senses.why: Keeping a memory is not only recalling it privately but also publicly refusing to let it fade.
senses.whyCN: 让记忆存续不只是私下回想，也是公开地拒绝让它淡去。

intro.en: Remember comes from Old French remembrer, from Latin rememorari, built on re- and memor, mindful.
intro.cn: remember 来自古法语 remembrer，源自拉丁语 rememorari，由 re- 与 memor「留心的、记得的」构成。

items.en: Memor means mindful or remembering, and gives memory, memorial, and memorable.
items.cn: memor 意为「留心的、记得的」，产生了 memory、memorial 与 memorable。

items.en: Rememorari means to recall or call back to mind, adding re- to memor.
items.cn: rememorari 意为回想、重新唤起记忆，在 memor 前加了 re-。

items.en: Remembrer means to recall and also to remind another person.
items.cn: 古法语 remembrer 既表示回想，也表示提醒别人。

items.en: English remember covers recall, keeping a duty in mind, and sending greetings.
items.cn: 英语 remember 覆盖回想、记住职责以及代问好等用法。

items.en: The public sense of honouring the dead grows out of the idea of keeping memory alive.
items.cn: 公开纪念逝者的义项，是从「让记忆继续存在」这一想法发展而来。

note.en: Remember belongs to the memor- family of memory and memorial, and it stands near remind and recall.
note.cn: remember 属于 memory、memorial 所在的 memor- 词族，并与 remind、recall 相邻。

entries.definition: the act of remembering or a thing kept in memory
entries.definitionCN: 记忆；纪念物，由 remember 加 -ance 构成

entries.definition: the ability to remember things
entries.definitionCN: 记忆力；回忆，与 remember 共享 memor 词根

entries.definition: worth remembering because it is special
entries.definitionCN: 难忘的；值得记住的

entries.definition: to bring something back into your mind
entries.definitionCN: 回想起，比 remember 更强调主动调取

entries.definition: to make someone remember something
entries.definitionCN: 提醒；使想起，方向相反

entries.definition: to learn something by heart
entries.definitionCN: 记住；背诵，强调刻意背下来

normalIntro.en: The memor- root of mindful is shared with memory and memorial, so the family is easy to keep together.
normalIntro.cn: 表示「留心」的 memor- 词根与 memory、memorial 共用，整族词很容易一起记。

normal.en: Re- plus memor, mindful, means becoming mindful again of something past.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 memor「留心的」，就是重新对过去的事留心。

normal.en: Remember to do looks forward, while remember doing looks back.
normal.cn: remember to do 指向将来，remember doing 指回过去。

normal.en: The noun remembrance adds -ance to the verb stem.
normal.cn: 名词 remembrance 在动词词干后加 -ance。

normal.en: Please remember me to your parents is a polite, slightly formal request.
normal.cn: 「please remember me to your parents」是礼貌而略正式的请求。

normal.en: Memory and memorable keep the same memor- stem without the re- prefix.
normal.cn: memory 与 memorable 保留同一个 memor- 词干，但不带 re- 前缀。

abstract.en: Picture an old photograph sliding out of a drawer, still sharp in every detail.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧照片从抽屉里滑出来，每个细节依旧清晰。

abstract.en: See a note tied to a door handle so the task cannot be missed.
abstract.cn: 想象门上系着一张纸条，让任务不会被漏掉。

abstract.en: Think of people standing quietly around a stone with names carved on it.
abstract.cn: 想人们安静地围着一块刻着名字的石头站着。

examples.en: I can't remember where I put the keys.
examples.cn: 我想不起来把钥匙放在哪里了。

examples.en: Remember to switch off the lights before you go.
examples.cn: 走之前记得关灯。

examples.en: The ceremony remembers those who died in the war.
examples.cn: 这场仪式纪念在战争中死去的人们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞曼伯」——想象瑞丽有位曼伯，能把往事一件件说清楚；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 remembrer，源自拉丁语 rememorari（re-「再次」+ memor「留心的、记得的」）。

sensesIntro.en: Keeping something mindful runs in four directions: what happened, what must be done, who should be greeted, and who must not be forgotten.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把某事放在心上」朝四个方向延伸：发生过什么、要做什么、该向谁问好、以及谁不能被忘记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a past scene returning with every detail intact.
core.cn: 核心意象：过去的场景带着完整细节重新浮现。

branches.en: Bringing a stored scene back is the central sense.
branches.cn: 把储存的场景重新调出，是这个词的中心义。

branches.en: Holding a future duty in mind points the same verb forward.
branches.cn: 把未来的职责放在心上，使这个动词指向前方。

branches.en: Holding a person in mind becomes a greeting sent through another.
branches.cn: 把某人放在心上，变成托人带去的问候。

branches.en: Publicly keeping a memory alive becomes commemoration.
branches.cn: 公开让记忆存续，就成为纪念。

branches.en: Private recall and public remembrance are two scales of one act.
branches.cn: 私下回想与公开纪念是同一个动作的两个尺度。

intro.en: Remember is a Latin-derived verb with a repeated prefix and a root about being mindful.
intro.cn: remember 是拉丁来源的动词，含表重复的前缀与表示「留心」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again, and memor means mindful, so the verb means to become mindful again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「再次」，memor 表示「留心的」，动词即「重新留心」。

items.example: Re- marks the return of a memory.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标记记忆的回返。

items.example: The memor- root also appears in memory.
items.exampleCN: memor- 词根也出现在 memory 中。

items.example: Memor is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整族词背后的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词词尾
items.example: Remembrance names the state of keeping someone in mind.
items.exampleCN: remembrance 指把某人放在心上的状态。

items.meaning: to recall, call back to mind
items.example: Rememorari is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: rememorari 是直接的拉丁祖先。

items.example: Memory and remember split the same stem.
items.exampleCN: memory 与 remember 分担同一个词干。

items.meaning: to honour the memory of someone
items.example: Commemorate adds com- to the same memor root.
items.exampleCN: commemorate 在同一个 memor 词根前加了 com-。

难忘的
纪念；缅怀

definition_zh: 宽慰；缓解；救济；浮雕；换班
definition_en: the good feeling that comes when pain, worry, or trouble stops or becomes less
core_image: 压在肩上的重物被突然搬走，人长长吐出一口气
scene: 手术室的灯灭后，医生摘下口罩说手术很成功，走廊里的人同时松下了肩膀。 When the doctor said the operation had succeeded, a wave of relief spread through the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 relief 是「宽慰、如释重负」（第 1 个义项：痛苦或忧虑解除后的轻松）；句意：医生说手术成功后，走廊里的人们感到一阵宽慰。

pos.zh: 宽慰；缓解；救济；浮雕；换班

derivatives.zh: 由名词 relief 回溯拉丁动词，义为「减轻；缓解」
relieve 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到宽慰的」
relieve 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed，义为「未获缓解的；单调的」

senses.title: The end of pain or worry
senses.definition: the pleasant feeling you have when pain, anxiety, or a difficult situation ends
senses.definitionCN: 疼痛、焦虑或困境结束后所产生的轻松愉快感
senses.example: She felt a huge sense of relief when the exam results finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩终于公布时，她感到如释重负。
senses.why: The Latin verb relevare means to raise or lift up, so the core image is a weight being lifted off the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 relevare 表示「抬起、举起」，所以核心画面是压在身上的重物被抬走，紧绷随之松开。

senses.title: Help for people in trouble
senses.definition: money, food, or other help given to people who are in need, especially after a disaster
senses.definitionCN: 给予困境中的人们的钱、食物或其他帮助，尤指灾后援助
senses.example: Relief supplies reached the village two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援物资运抵了村庄。
senses.why: If the core image is lifting a weight, then lifting people out of hardship naturally gives the word the sense of aid itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心画面是把重物抬起，那么把人从苦难中托起来，就自然延伸出「援助」这一义项。

senses.title: A design raised above a surface
senses.definition: a design cut into stone or metal so that it stands out above the flat background
senses.definitionCN: 在石头或金属上雕刻出的、凸出于平面的图案
senses.example: The coin shows the queen's head in relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚硬币上铸有女王头像的浮雕。
senses.why: The raised part of a carving is literally lifted above the surface, which matches the lifting image at the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕凸起的部分正是从平面被「抬起来」的，与这个词核心的抬起画面完全吻合。

senses.title: A shift that takes over a duty
senses.definition: a person or group that takes over a job from someone else so that the work can continue
senses.definitionCN: 从他人手中接过工作、使工作中断得以继续的人或班组
senses.example: The night relief arrived at six in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班接替人员早上六点到了。
senses.why: Passing a load from one pair of shoulders to another is the same lifting picture, applied to work shifts.
senses.whyCN: 把重担从一副肩膀交到另一副肩膀，仍是「抬起并转移」这个画面，用在轮班场景里就成了换班。

intro.en: Relief comes through Old French from the Latin verb relevare, built from the prefix re- and the verb levare.
intro.cn: relief 经由古法语来自拉丁动词 relevare，该词由前缀 re- 与动词 levare 组合而成。

items.en: Relevare means to raise up, lift, or lighten, and is formed from re- plus levare.
items.cn: relevare 意为抬起、举起或减轻，由 re- 与 levare 构成。

items.en: Levare comes from the adjective levis, light in weight, the same root found in levity.
items.cn: levare 源自形容词 levis「重量轻的」，这个词根也见于 levity。

items.en: Relevium names a payment raised from a tenant, showing the idea of something lifted up.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 relevium 指向佃户征收的一笔款项，同样带有「被抬起之物」的意味。

items.en: Old French relief carries the senses of a raising, of help, and of a remainder.
items.cn: 古法语 relief 同时有「抬起」「帮助」「剩余部分」几层意思。

items.en: English borrows the word for help given to someone in trouble and for a raised carving.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用于表示给予困境中人的帮助，也指凸起的雕刻。

items.en: Modern English keeps the eased feeling, the aid, the raised carving, and the relieving shift.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了宽慰感、援助、浮雕以及换班这几层含义。

note.en: Relief belongs to a re- and lev- family about lifting weight, and it sits near words for making trouble smaller.
note.cn: relief 属于由 re- 与 lev- 构成、表示「抬起重量」的词族，同时又与表示「使麻烦变小」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to make pain or a problem less serious
entries.definitionCN: 缓解；减轻，是 relief 对应的动词形式

entries.definition: feeling glad that a worry or pain has gone
entries.definitionCN: 感到宽慰的，由 relieve 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: a lack of seriousness, often in a situation that needs it
entries.definitionCN: 轻浮；轻率，与 relief 共享 levis「轻」的词根

entries.definition: a pleasant feeling of being free from pain or worry
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；安慰，侧重身心放松的状态

entries.definition: the state of feeling no pain, difficulty, or worry
entries.definitionCN: 轻松；安逸，强调没有负担

entries.definition: help, especially money or goods given to people in need
entries.definitionCN: 援助；救助，与 relief 的第二义项接近

normalIntro.en: The word is built on Latin levare, to lift, so the memory hooks mostly involve lifting a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语 levare「举起」之上，所以记忆钩子大多围绕「把重物抬走」。

normal.en: Re- plus lev- gives the picture of lifting something up again, and the weight comes off.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加词根 lev-，画面是把东西重新抬起来，重量随之离开。

normal.en: Compare elevator: both words lift, one lifts people, the other lifts weight off a mind.
normal.cn: 对比 elevator：两者都在「抬起」，一个载人，一个把重量从心头抬走。

normal.en: The pair relief and relieve differs only by the last letter, noun against verb.
normal.cn: relief 与 relieve 只差最后一个字母，一个是名词，一个是动词。

normal.en: A sigh of relief is literally the sound of a lifted weight.
normal.cn: a sigh of relief 字面上就是重物被抬走时那口长气。

normal.en: Disaster relief is help that lifts a whole town back onto its feet.
normal.cn: disaster relief 是把整座城镇重新托起来的援助。

abstract.en: Imagine a backpack of stones sliding off your back; your shoulders drop and you breathe out.
abstract.cn: 想象一包石头从背上滑落，肩膀塌下来，你长长呼气。

abstract.en: Think of a carved coin: the head is pushed up out of the flat metal.
abstract.cn: 想一枚硬币，头像被从平整的金属里顶出来。

abstract.en: Picture a relay of workers: one steps away, the next takes the load.
abstract.cn: 想象工人接力：一个人退下，下一个人接过重物。

examples.en: She breathed a sigh of relief when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她松了一口气。

examples.en: The government sent relief to the flooded region.
examples.cn: 政府向洪涝地区运送了救援物资。

examples.en: The statue is carved in relief on the temple wall.
examples.cn: 庙墙上雕着这座雕像的浮雕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽福」——想象瑞丽小城送来福气，紧绷的心一下松开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次、向后）+ levare（举起，源自 levis「轻」）构成 relevare（抬起、减轻），经古法语 relief 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One image of a lifted weight grows into four senses: the eased mind, the aid given, the raised carving, and the shift that takes over.
sensesIntro.cn: 「抬起重量」这一个画面长出四个义项：心里的轻松、给出的援助、凸起的浮雕，以及接过工作的换班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy weight lifted from the shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在肩上的重物被抬起搬走。

branches.en: The mind feels the weight go, so relief names the eased feeling.
branches.cn: 心里感到重量消失，于是 relief 指那种松弛下来的感觉。

branches.en: Lifting a person out of hardship becomes the name for the help itself.
branches.cn: 把人从困境中托起来，进一步成为「援助」的名称。

branches.en: A carving stands up above the flat surface, exactly like something lifted.
branches.cn: 浮雕高出平面，正像被抬起的东西。

branches.en: A load passed to fresh hands becomes the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 重担交到新的人手上，就成了接替的班次。

branches.en: Both the eased feeling and the aid come from the same upward movement.
branches.cn: 心中的松弛与外来的援助都源自同一个向上的动作。

intro.en: Relief is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin root, with a French noun ending carried into English.
intro.cn: relief 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根以及传入英语的法语名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin prefix re- means back or again, and levare means to lift, so together they describe lifting a burden away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「向后、再次」，levare 表示「举起」，合起来就是「把重担抬走」。

items.example: The prefix re- returns in relieve and remove.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 relieve 与 remove 中。

items.example: The root lev- also appears in elevate and levity.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lev- 也出现在 elevate 与 levity 中。

items.example: Levare is the verb behind relief and relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 是 relief 与 relieve 背后的动词。

items.example: Levis is the source of the lev- root in this family.
items.exampleCN: levis 是这一词族中 lev- 词根的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -ief carries the French form into English relief.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ief 把法语形式带进了英语 relief。

items.meaning: to lift up again, to ease
items.example: Relevare joins re- and levare into a single verb.
items.exampleCN: relevare 把 re- 与 levare 合成了一个动词。

items.example: Levity uses the same levis root for lightness of behaviour.
items.exampleCN: levity 用同一个 levis 词根表示举止上的轻。

items.example: Alleviate adds ad- to the same levis root.
items.exampleCN: alleviate 在同一个 levis 词根前加了 ad-。

definition_zh: 原因；起因；事业；导致；引起
definition_en: the reason something happens, a principle people fight for, or to make something happen
core_image: 第一块倒下的多米诺骨牌，推倒了后面一整排
scene: 实验课后，大家一起讨论这次泡沫喷发的原因。 After the experiment the class discussed the cause of the foam eruption.
sceneCN: 这里 cause 是「原因」（第 1 个义项：使某事发生的东西）；句意为课后讨论泡沫喷发的原因。

derivatives.zh: 由 by + cause 构成，义为「因为」
同根词，义为「借口；理由」

senses.title: The reason something happens
senses.definition: the person, event or thing that makes something happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的人、事件或事物
senses.example: Heavy rain was the cause of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨是洪水的原因。
senses.why: Latin causa meant a reason argued in court, and the courtroom reason became the everyday one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 指庭上争辩的理由，这理由走下法庭便成了日常的「原因」。

senses.title: A principle worth supporting
senses.definition: a principle or aim that people support or fight for
senses.definitionCN: 人们支持或为之奋斗的原则与目标
senses.example: They raised money for an environmental cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为环保事业筹款。
senses.why: A reason you argue for in court is also a side you take; the reason became a banner.
senses.whyCN: 庭上所争之由，也是你所站的一边，理由就此变成旗帜。

senses.title: To make something happen
senses.definition: to make something happen, especially something bad
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生，多指坏事
senses.example: The storm caused several road accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨引发多起车祸。
senses.why: What stands behind an event is also what pushes it into being, so the noun grew a verb.
senses.whyCN: 立于事件之后者，也是把它推进存在者，名词于是长出了动词。

intro.en: Cause descends from a Latin word for a reason or lawsuit.
intro.cn: cause 源自拉丁语中表示「理由或诉讼」的词。

items.en: Latin causa meant reason, motive and legal case at once.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 一词兼指理由、动机与案件。

items.en: Old French chose and later cause carried the legal reason sense.
items.cn: 古法语 chose 后作 cause，保留法律理由义。

items.en: Middle English cause covered reasons, sides in court and aims.
items.cn: 中古英语 cause 涵盖理由、诉讼立场与目标。

items.en: Its deeper root is uncertain; some link it to cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 更深词根存疑，一说与 cadere（落下）相关。

items.en: Modern cause gained the verb and the charity sense.
items.cn: 现代 cause 增加了动词用法与公益之义。

note.en: The first group collects same-root words; the second collects reason-and-effect words.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收因果类词。

entries.definition: For the reason that.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「因为」，字面即 by cause。

entries.definition: A reason offered to explain or forgive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「借口」，同出拉丁 causa 族。

entries.definition: A path of study or a route.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「课程；路线」，拼写与 cause 相近。

entries.definition: Why something happens or is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理由；缘故」。

entries.definition: The result of a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，与原因相对。

entries.definition: The thing that sets an event off.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「触发因素」。

normalIntro.en: Remember cause through its courtroom past.
normalIntro.cn: 借法庭往事记忆 cause。

normal.en: cause comes from Latin causa, a legal reason.
normal.cn: cause 源自拉丁语 causa（诉讼理由）。

normal.en: because is literally by cause.
normal.cn: because 字面就是 by cause。

normal.en: excuse is its soft cousin, a small reason.
normal.cn: excuse 是它的温和表亲，一个小理由。

normal.en: cause trouble means to create trouble.
normal.cn: cause trouble 即惹麻烦。

normal.en: a good cause is work worth donating to.
normal.cn: good cause 值得捐助。

abstract.en: Watch the first domino lean and the whole line go.
abstract.cn: 看第一张骨牌一倾，整排连锁倒下。

abstract.en: Trace the crack in the cup back to its sudden slip.
abstract.cn: 顺着杯子上的裂纹找回那次脱手。

abstract.en: Feel a small stone start a big roll downhill.
abstract.cn: 一块小石头启动了滚下山的巨石。

examples.en: Scientists are still studying the cause of the illness.
examples.cn: 科学家仍在研究这种疾病的病因。

examples.en: Careless smoking caused the forest fire.
examples.cn: 疏忽的吸烟引发了森林火灾。

examples.en: Every student joined the charity cause.
examples.cn: 每位学生都参与了这项慈善事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「叩斯」——敲叩一下，事情由此而起。

root: 拉丁语 causa（理由；诉讼）→ 古法语 cause → 英语 cause；同族 because、excuse、accuse（控告，同根不同源支）。

sensesIntro.en: Cause holds a courtroom reason, a banner to follow and the push behind events.
sensesIntro.cn: cause 同时握着庭上的理由、高举的旗帜与事件背后的推力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first push before everything else moves
core.cn: 核心意象：一切运动之前的那一推

branches.en: Why things happen
branches.cn: 事情为何发生

branches.en: Ideas people march behind
branches.cn: 人们追随的理念

branches.en: Making bad things happen
branches.cn: 酿成不好的结果

branches.en: Science looks for causes
branches.cn: 科学寻找原因

branches.en: Standing behind an outcome
branches.cn: 站在某个后果背后

intro.en: Cause is a single root whose endings made several everyday words.
intro.cn: cause 是单一词根，其后缀生出了几个日常词。

latinIntro.en: Latin causa stayed almost unchanged through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 causa 经法语进入英语，几乎未变。

items.exampleCN: causa 开启每一场罗马庭审。
because 由 by 与 cause 拼合。

items.example: He stayed home because of the rain.
He made an excuse and left.

items.meaning: the relation of cause and effect

items.exampleCN: 没有真正无缘无故的怒火。

items.meaning: a fight that cannot be won
items.example: Fixing that old bike is a lost cause.

definition_zh: 柠檬；柠檬树；柠檬味；无用的东西（尤指有缺陷的汽车）
definition_en: a yellow citrus fruit with sour juice; the tree that bears it; its flavour; something that proves defective, especially a car
core_image: 黄皮酸果，一口把人酸得眯起眼
scene: 夏日午后，她切了两片黄果放进冰水。 Fresh lemon makes the tea taste brighter.
sceneCN: 这里 lemon 是「水果」（第 1 个义项：柠檬果）；句意为鲜柠檬让茶喝起来更清爽。

derivatives.zh: lemon 加 -y，指「柠檬味的；柠檬色的」
lemon 加 -ade 饮料后缀，指「柠檬水」

senses.title: The sour yellow fruit
senses.definition: a yellow oval citrus fruit with very sour juice
senses.definitionCN: 黄色椭圆的柑橘类水果，汁极酸
senses.example: She squeezed half a lemon over the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她在鱼上挤了半个柠檬的汁。
senses.why: The fruit itself is the root picture: yellow skin, sharp juice, unmistakable smell.
senses.whyCN: 果实本身就是根意象：黄皮、酸汁、 unmistakable 的气味。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: the evergreen tree that produces lemons
senses.definitionCN: 长柠檬的常绿树
senses.example: Their garden has two lemon trees.
senses.exampleCN: 他们园里有两棵柠檬树。
senses.why: The fruit names the plant that carries it, as English often does.
senses.whyCN: 果名为树命名，这是英语的常态。

senses.title: The flavour or colour
senses.definition: the sharp flavour of lemon, or its pale yellow colour
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬的酸香风味，或其淡黄色
senses.example: The cake has a lemon flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个蛋糕有柠檬味。
senses.why: The fruit is so distinct that taste and colour borrow its name.
senses.whyCN: 果实特征鲜明，味与色都借它的名字。

senses.title: A defective product
senses.definition: something bought that turns out faulty, especially a car
senses.definitionCN: 买来后发现有问题之物，尤指汽车
senses.example: That used car turned out to be a lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆二手车结果是辆次品车。
senses.why: A sour fruit stands for a sour deal: sweet promises, bitter outcome.
senses.whyCN: 酸果代表酸涩的交易：承诺甜，结果苦。

senses.title: A silly or disappointing person
senses.titleCN: 傻里傻气或令人失望的人
senses.definition: a person who behaves foolishly or is a disappointment
senses.definitionCN: 行为傻气或让人失望的人
senses.example: Don\u2019t be such a lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯傻了。
senses.why: Calling a person a lemon keeps the sour, useless shade of the fruit.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作 lemon，保留了果实酸涩无用的色彩。

senses.title: A drink made with lemon
senses.definition: a drink flavoured or mixed with lemon juice
senses.definitionCN: 用柠檬汁调味或调制的饮品
senses.example: Two iced lemons, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请来两杯冰柠檬饮。
senses.why: Products take the name of the fruit that defines them.
senses.whyCN: 产品以定义它的水果为名。

intro.en: Lemon came into English through Old French and Medieval Latin limon, likely from Arabic laymun, which itself came from Persian.
intro.cn: lemon 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语 limon 进入英语，可能源自阿拉伯语 laymun，而后者又来自波斯语。

items.en: Persian limun is the likely starting point, naming the citrus fruit long traded in Asia.
items.cn: 波斯语 limun 很可能是起点，命名了亚洲长期贸易的柑橘果。

items.en: Arabic laymun carried the fruit and the word westward with trade.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 laymun 带着果实与词语随贸易西行。

items.en: Medieval Latin limon appears in European texts, keeping the trade route visible.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 limon 见于欧洲文献，贸易路线依稀可见。

items.en: Old French lemon brought the word across the Channel in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中古晚期，古法语 lemon 把词渡过了海峡。

items.en: Modern English kept lemon for the fruit and later coined the defective-product sense in American slang.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lemon 指果实，后来美国俚语又造出「次品」义。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects sour and citrus words.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集酸味与柑橘之词。

entries.definition: Lemon plus the drink suffix -ade.
entries.definitionCN: lemon 加饮品后缀 -ade。

entries.definition: A sweet gourd fruit; shares letters but the root is separate.
entries.definitionCN: 甜瓜；字母相叠，词根不同。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 同词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: The green citrus, sharper and smaller than a lemon.
entries.definitionCN: 青柠，比柠檬更小更尖。

entries.definition: The sweet citrus, sharing the same trade history.
entries.definitionCN: 甜橙，同样有贸易史。

entries.definition: The large tart citrus of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 同族中较大较酸的柚类。

entries.definition: Slang for something that fails, matching the defective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 俚语「失败品」，对应次品义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real borrowings and the slang sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实借词链与俚语义。

normal.en: The trail runs Persian limun, Arabic laymun, Medieval Latin limon, Old French lemon.
normal.cn: 词路：波斯语 limun → 阿拉伯语 laymun → 中世纪拉丁语 limon → 古法语 lemon。

normal.en: Family: lemony, lemonade.
normal.cn: 词族：lemony、lemonade。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: lemon juice, lemon tree, lemon yellow.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：柠檬汁、柠檬树、柠檬黄。

normal.en: American slang calls a bad car a lemon.
normal.cn: 美国俚语把问题车叫作 lemon。

normal.en: When life gives you lemons is a proverb about turning trouble into good.
normal.cn: 「生活给你柠檬」是化苦为甜的谚语。

abstract.en: Picture your face puckering after one tiny sip.
abstract.cn: 想象小小一口之后整张脸皱起来。

abstract.en: Picture a shiny car that sputters the day after you buy it.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆光鲜的车，买回第二天就熄火。

abstract.en: Picture sour fruit squeezed into sweet tea, trouble turned useful.
abstract.cn: 想象酸果挤进甜茶，麻烦变得有用。

examples.en: Add a slice of lemon to the water and it tastes fresher.
examples.cn: 水里加一片柠檬，喝起来更清新。

examples.en: The market sells lemons from the south in winter.
examples.cn: 市场冬天卖南方来的柠檬。

examples.en: He complained that the laptop he bought was a lemon.
examples.cn: 他抱怨买来的笔记本是台次品。

root: 一般认为经阿拉伯语 laymun 追溯至波斯语 limun，再经中世纪拉丁语 limon 与古法语 lemon 进入英语；具体波斯语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses move from the fruit itself to its tree, taste, colour, drinks, and finally to sour deals and people.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从果实本身走向树、味、色、饮品，最后落到酸涩的交易与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sour yellow fruit that puckers your mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸得让人皱嘴的黄果。

branches.en: THE PLANT: fruit and the tree that bears it.
branches.cn: 植物：果实与结果之树。

branches.en: TASTE AND TASTE PRODUCTS: flavour, colour, and lemon drinks.
branches.cn: 味与味的产品：风味、颜色与柠檬饮。

branches.en: SOUR TRANSFER: sourness spread to bad products and silly people.
branches.cn: 酸的转移：酸味扩散到次品与傻人。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: every sense keeps the sharp yellow profile.
branches.cn: 轴心：每个义项都保留黄而酸的轮廓。

branches.en: NAMED BY SOURCE: colour takes the fruit\u2019s name.
branches.cn: 以源命名：颜色借果名。

intro.en: Lemon is a borrowed noun with no English affixes of its own; derivatives attach English suffixes to it.
intro.cn: lemon 是无英语词缀的外来名词；派生词是在其上附加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognate is established, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native suffix work on a loanword.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示外来词上的本族后缀加工。

definition_zh: 地方；地点；座位；名次；放置
definition_en: a particular position or area; a seat kept for one person; a rank in a competition; and to put something in a particular position
core_image: 广场中央空出的一块干净石板地
scene: 集市散去的午后，广场上腾出一大片石板地。 She stood in the middle of the empty market place and listened to the pigeons.
sceneCN: 这里 place 是「地方、地点」（第 1 个义项：某个具体的位置或区域）；句意为她站在空下来的集市空地上，听着鸽子叫。图中可辨识物件：石板地、空摊位、几只鸽子。

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 re-（回、再）加 place 构成，义为「放回原处；取代」
由前缀 dis-（离开）加 place 构成，义为「使离开原位；迫使迁移」
由 place 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「安置；安排的位置」

senses.title: A particular position or area
senses.definition: a particular position, area or spot, especially one used for a stated purpose
senses.definitionCN: 某一个具体的位置、区域或地点，尤指有特定用途的地方
senses.example: This is a good place to stop for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这是个过夜的好地方。
senses.why: Latin platea named a broad open street, and an open surface is the first thing the eye can point at; from any open area the word narrowed to one particular spot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 platea 原指宽阔的露天街道，露天的面是最先能被指认的东西；词义于是从任意一片空地收窄为某一个具体地点。

senses.title: A seat or position kept for someone
senses.definition: a seat, space or position reserved for one person, as at a table or in a queue
senses.definitionCN: 在桌边或队伍里为某一个人留出的座位、空间或位置
senses.example: Please keep my place at the table while I get some water.
senses.exampleCN: 我去倒水的时候，请帮我留着桌边的位子。
senses.why: Once a wide surface can be divided among the people standing on it, a share of that surface can be held for one person, and place comes to mean a reserved seat.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的场地一旦被站在上面的人划分开来，其中一份就能为某个人留着，place 因此有了「预留座位」的意思。

senses.title: A rank in a competition
senses.definition: the position someone finishes in a race or competition, counted from the winner
senses.definitionCN: 某人在赛跑或比赛中到达终点的位次，从冠军开始数
senses.example: Our team finished in second place.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队获得了第二名。
senses.why: A race turns open ground into a line of positions, and the order in which runners reach the finish gives each one a place in the ranking.
senses.whyCN: 赛跑把开阔的场地变成一排有先后的位置，跑者到达终点的次序就给每个人定下了名次。

senses.title: To put something in a position
senses.definition: to put something in a particular position, or to arrange it there deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在某个特定位置，或有意把它安排在那里
senses.example: He placed the vase carefully on the windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心地把花瓶放在窗台上。
senses.why: The verb comes straight from the noun: to place an object is to give it the spot that the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接从名词而来：place 一样东西，就是给它一个名词所指的位置。

intro.en: Place goes back to a Greek word for a broad way, which Latin borrowed for a wide street and French narrowed to an open square and then to any spot.
intro.cn: place 上溯到希腊语中表示「宽阔道路」的词，拉丁语借来指宽街，法语把它收窄为开阔的广场，再收窄为任何一个地点。

items.en: Greek plateia, short for plateia hodos, meant a broad way, and it was built on platys, broad.
items.cn: 希腊语 plateia 是 plateia hodos 的省略，意为宽阔的道路，建立在 platys（宽的）之上。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as platea, a broad street or an open court.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词借作 platea，指宽阔的街道或露天的庭院。

items.en: Old French place named an open space or square in a town, and also a spot or a position.
items.cn: 古法语 place 指城镇里的空地、广场，也指某个地点或位置。

items.en: Middle English place covered open ground, a spot, and a person's rank or standing.
items.cn: 中古英语的 place 兼指空地、地点，以及一个人的身份地位。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spot, adds the reserved seat and the finishing rank, and uses place as a verb of putting.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「地点」，加上预留座位与比赛名次，并让 place 作动词表示放置。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for a broad open space and three words that merely share its letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for a position or a site.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示开阔场地的拉丁词展开，另收三个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示位置与地点的词。

entries.definition: A public square or market area; Spanish kept the Latin word for a broad open space.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场或集市空地；西班牙语保留了拉丁语里表示开阔场地的这个词。

entries.definition: A flat dish or sheet; it looks like place but comes from another Romance word for something flat, so the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 平盘或平板；拼写与 place 相近，却来自另一个表示扁平物的罗曼语词，词源不同。

entries.definition: A raised area of flat land; the resemblance is in spelling only, and the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 高原；只是拼写相像，来源不同。

entries.definition: A body orbiting a star; Greek planan, to wander, is behind it, not the root of place.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行的天体；背后是希腊语 planan（漫游），并非 place 的词根。

entries.definition: A particular place where something is or happens.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所在或某事发生的特定地方。

entries.definition: A small area or a particular point on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块地方，或表面上某个具体的点。

entries.definition: The place where someone or something is, or a rank in an order.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物所在的位置，也指次序中的名次。

entries.definition: A place where a building stands or where an event happened.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑所在或事件发生的地点。

normalIntro.en: The word began as open ground that anyone could point at, and its family keeps three pictures: a square, a spot held for someone, and a numbered position.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从谁都能指出的开阔场地开始，词族里保留着三幅画面：广场、为某人留着的位置，以及编了号的位次。

normal.en: Greek plateia meant a broad way, and Latin platea kept that open street, so the oldest picture is a wide surface underfoot.
normal.cn: 希腊语 plateia 意为宽阔的道路，拉丁语 platea 保留了这条开阔的街，所以最古老的画面是脚下的一大片地面。

normal.en: Old French place already meant both a town square and a spot, and English kept both, which is why a public square and a seat can share the word.
normal.cn: 古法语 place 已经同时指城镇广场和某个地点，英语两者都保留，所以广场和座位能共用一个词。

normal.en: Replace is re- plus place, to put back; displace is dis- plus place, to drive something away from its place.
normal.cn: replace 是 re- 加 place，表示放回；displace 是 dis- 加 place，表示把东西赶离原位。

normal.en: Take place means happen, because an event takes its spot in time the way an object takes its spot on the ground.
normal.cn: take place 意为发生，因为一件事像物体占地一样，在时间里占住自己的位置。

normal.en: The verb is regular: places, placed, placing, and the silent e is dropped before -ing.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：places、placed、placing，词尾不发音的 e 在 -ing 前去掉。

abstract.en: A place is not a thing but a promise that a thing can be found there.
abstract.cn: 地点本身不是东西，而是一个承诺：在那里能找到某样东西。

abstract.en: To hold a place for someone is to turn empty space into a small piece of waiting.
abstract.cn: 为某人留一个位置，就是把空地变成一小块等待。

abstract.en: First place and last place describe the same track; only the order of arrival makes the difference.
abstract.cn: 第一名和最后一名描述的是同一条跑道，区别只在到达的先后。

examples.en: This is a good place to stop for the night.
examples.cn: 这是个过夜的好地方。

examples.en: Our team finished in second place.
examples.cn: 我们队获得了第二名。

examples.en: He placed the vase carefully on the windowsill.
examples.cn: 他小心地把花瓶放在窗台上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺来石」——地上铺来石板，就成了一个地方；记住 place 是地方。

root: 希腊语 plateia（宽阔的道路）经拉丁语 platea（宽街、露天庭院）与古法语 place（广场、地点）进入英语；西班牙语 plaza 保留了同一个拉丁词「开阔场地」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open surface that can be pointed at; the senses run from a particular spot, to a seat reserved for one person, to a rank in a race, and finally to the act of putting something there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一片能被指认的开阔地面；义项从具体地点，走到为某人留的座位，再到比赛名次，最后落到把东西放到那里这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear patch of stone in the middle of a busy square.
core.cn: 核心意象：热闹广场中央一块干净的石板地。

branches.en: an empty market square at midday
branches.cn: 正午空下来的集市广场

branches.en: a chair pulled out for a guest at the table
branches.cn: 为客人拉开的椅子

branches.en: a coat on a chair keeping a seat for someone
branches.cn: 搭在椅上替人占位的外套

branches.en: a runner crossing the line second
branches.cn: 第二个冲过终点的跑者

branches.en: a vase set down on a windowsill
branches.cn: 搁在窗台上的花瓶

intro.en: The word is a Romance borrowing built on a Greek adjective for broad, and English prefixes and suffixes then turn it into verbs and a noun of arrangement.
intro.cn: 这个词是罗曼语借词，建立在表示「宽阔」的希腊形容词上，英语的前缀与后缀随后把它变成动词和一个表示安置的名词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin noun is recorded behind this word: platea, the broad street that Greek supplied and French later narrowed to a square.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有一个可考的拉丁名词 platea，即希腊语提供、后来被法语收窄为广场的那条宽街。

definition_zh: 加入；连接；参加；把……接起来；会合
definition_en: to become a member of a group, or to fasten two or more things together so that they touch or form one thing
core_image: 两块木料被一道榫头咬合在一起，接缝看不出来
scene: 社团招新的长桌摆在广场中央，路过的人停下填表。 Over a hundred students joined the club in its first week.
sceneCN: 这里 join 是「加入」（第 1 个义项：成为某个团体的成员），句意为社团成立第一周就有一百多名学生加入。画面里的物件：长桌、表格、广场。

pos.zh: 动词：加入；参加；连接；会合

derivatives.zh: 由 join 加 -t 构成，指接合处或关节
由 joint 加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地、连带地」
由 join 加 -er 构成，义为「细木工匠」
由 join 加 -ing 构成，义为「连接；接合处」
加 en- 前缀构成，义为「责令；禁止」

senses.title: To become a member
senses.definition: to become a member of a group, club, company, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个团体、社团、公司或组织的成员
senses.example: She joined the debating society in her first term.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一个学期加入了辩论社。
senses.why: Membership is a joining of oneself to a body, the same act as joining two things.
senses.whyCN: 加入就是把自己接到一个群体上，与把两样东西接起来是同一个动作。

senses.title: To fasten things together
senses.definition: to fasten two or more things so that they are linked or become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或多个东西接在一起，使其相连或成为一体
senses.example: Join the two pipes with a short metal collar.
senses.exampleCN: 用一段短金属箍把两根管子接起来。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical layer: two edges brought to touch.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理层含义：两条边被凑到一起。

senses.title: To take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in something that others are already doing
senses.definitionCN: 参与别人已经在做的事
senses.example: Do come and join the game after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后一定来参加游戏。
senses.why: Taking part is joining one activity rather than one organization.
senses.whyCN: 参加指的是加入一项活动，而不是一个组织。

senses.title: To meet and merge
senses.definition: to meet and combine, as roads, rivers, or people on a route
senses.definitionCN: 指道路、河流或路上的人在一点汇合
senses.example: The two paths join just below the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两条小路就在桥下会合。
senses.why: Two lines meeting is the physical joining seen from the path itself.
senses.whyCN: 两条线交汇，就是站在路的角度看的「接合」。

senses.title: To share in a feeling or action
senses.definition: to share an action or feeling with someone, often in a set phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中与他人共同做某事或共有某种感受
senses.example: The whole hall joined in the chorus.
senses.exampleCN: 全场一起唱起了副歌。
senses.why: Joining a voice to others extends the fastener image to sound and feeling.
senses.whyCN: 把自己的声音接到别人那里，是把接合的画面延伸到声音与情绪上。

intro.en: Join comes from French joindre, from Latin jungere, "to yoke or connect"; the same root gives junction and jugular.
intro.cn: join 来自法语 joindre，源于拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」；同一词根还生出 junction、jugular。

items.en: jungere meant to join or yoke animals together, from jugum, a yoke.
items.cn: jungere 意为把牲口套在一起，源自 jugum「轭」。

items.en: junctus was its past participle, giving the stem junct- seen in junction.
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 给出 junct- 词干，见于 junction。

items.en: Old French joindre softened the consonant and dropped the nasal ending in speech.
items.cn: 古法语 joindre 软化了辅音，口语里还丢了鼻音词尾。

items.en: English borrowed join in the thirteenth century for both uniting and becoming a member.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 join，既指连接也指成为成员。

items.en: Join up and join in fixed the phrasal uses in later centuries.
items.cn: join up 与 join in 在后几个世纪固定为短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jung- stem; the near-meaning group holds verbs for connecting and taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁词干 jung-；近义组收表示连接与参与的词。

entries.definition: A place where two parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指接合处或关节。

entries.definition: A point where things meet, especially roads.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指交汇处，尤指路口。

entries.definition: A craftsman who makes wooden joints.
entries.definitionCN: 由 join 加 -er 构成，指细木工匠。

entries.definition: To link two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，语气更中性。

entries.definition: To go into a place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「进入」，强调走进去。

entries.definition: To register as a member of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指注册入学或入会。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin yoke to the club table on the square.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「轭」走到广场上的招新长桌。

normal.en: Latin jungere meant to yoke animals together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 意为把牲口套在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives joint, junction, and juncture.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 joint、junction、juncture。

normal.en: Join a club takes a direct object with no preposition.
normal.cn: join a club 直接跟宾语，不加介词。

normal.en: Join in is used for activities rather than organizations.
normal.cn: join in 用于活动，而不是组织。

normal.en: Join forces means two sides put their strength together.
normal.cn: join forces 指双方把力量合在一起。

abstract.en: To join is to put two edges so close the seam disappears.
abstract.cn: 加入就是把两条边贴到接缝合拢。

abstract.en: A yoke over two necks is the oldest picture of the word.
abstract.cn: 横在两条脖子上的轭，是这个词最老的画面。

abstract.en: Every member is one more thread tied to the same rope.
abstract.cn: 每个成员都是系在同一根绳上的又一根线。

examples.en: He joined the company as a junior clerk.
examples.cn: 他作为初级职员加入了这家公司。

examples.en: Join the two wires and wrap them with tape.
examples.cn: 把两根线接上，再用胶布缠好。

examples.en: Will you join us for lunch?
examples.cn: 你跟我们一起去吃午饭吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佐因」—— 佐理的人进来，就是加入

root: 拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」（源自 jugum「轭」）→ 过去分词 junctus → 古法语 joindre → 英语 join。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: becoming a member, fastening things, taking part, meeting and merging, and sharing in an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：成为成员、把东西接起来、参加活动、会合，以及一同参与。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges brought together until the seam cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边被凑到一起，直到看不见接缝。

branches.en: THE CLUB TABLE: a name written on a list of members.
branches.cn: 招新桌这条线：名字写进会员名单。

branches.en: THE PIPE LINE: two ends fitted into one collar.
branches.cn: 管子这条线：两个端头套进同一个箍。

branches.en: THE GAME LINE: stepping in while others already play.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：别人已经在玩时走进去。

branches.en: THE CROSSROADS: two paths becoming one below the bridge.
branches.cn: 路口这条线：两条路在桥下合成一条。

branches.en: THE CHORUS: one voice added to many.
branches.cn: 合唱这条线：一个声音加进许多声音。

intro.en: Join carries the Latin stem jung- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: join 带着拉丁词干 jung-，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jungere, to yoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jungere「套轭」。

items.meaning: to connect or become a member

definition_zh: 中间；中部；中期；腰部；中间的；中等的；中间派的
definition_en: the central point or part of something, the middle period of a process, the waist, or an adjective meaning central or moderate
core_image: 一条长桌的正中摆着一只花瓶，两侧的椅子对称排开
scene: 长桌两端都坐满了人，只有正中的位置还空着，等着最后到的那位客人。 She cut the cake down the middle and gave half to each child.
sceneCN: 这里 middle 是「中间、正中」（第 1 个义项：距离两边同样远的位置）；句意为她沿着正中把蛋糕切开，分给每个孩子一半。画面里可抓住的物件：长桌、空着的正中座位、切开的蛋糕。

pos.zh: 中间的；中等的；中间派的

derivatives.zh: 由 middle 加 -ing 构成，义为「中等的、还过得去的」
由 middle 与 man 复合，义为「中间商；中介」
由 middle 与 weight 复合，指拳击的中量级
由 middle 与 brow 复合，指品味中庸的（人）

senses.title: The central point or part
senses.definition: the point or area equally far from the edges or ends of something
senses.definitionCN: 距离边缘或两端同样远的那一点或那一带
senses.example: There is a fountain in the middle of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场中央有一座喷泉。
senses.why: Old English middel was built with the suffix -el from a root for middle, much as a small tool is made from a larger one; the word names the place that divides a length into equal halves.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 middel 由表示「中间」的词根加后缀 -el 构成，就像用一个较大物件做出小工具；这个词指的就是把一段长度分成相等两半的位置。

senses.title: The middle of a period or process
senses.definition: a point in time when an event or process is half done
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件或过程进行到一半的时间点
senses.example: The project ran into trouble in the middle of the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目在夏季中期遇到了麻烦。
senses.why: Because the central point can be laid on time as well as on space, the same word covers the halfway stage of a season, a story or a negotiation.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个中心点既能放在空间上，也能放在时间上，同一个词便覆盖了季节、故事或谈判进行到一半的阶段。

senses.title: The waist
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body between the chest and the hips, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指胸部与臀部之间身体较窄的部分
senses.example: He tied the rope around his middle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子系在腰上。
senses.why: A body is widest at the shoulders and hips and narrows between them, so the word for the central part came to name the waist with no metaphor beyond shape.
senses.whyCN: 人的身体在肩与臀处最宽，中间收窄，于是表示「中部」的词就用来指腰，除了形状之外并没有额外的比喻。

senses.title: Halfway between two positions
senses.definition: placed or ranked between two other things, neither first nor last
senses.definitionCN: 处在另外两者之间，既不在最前也不在最后
senses.example: Put the tallest child in the middle row.
senses.exampleCN: 把最高的孩子安排在中间那一排。
senses.why: The noun turned adjective by standing before another noun; middle row simply means the row that sits between the front and the back.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前面就转成了形容词；middle row 指的就是夹在最前与最后之间的那一排。

senses.title: Moderate in politics or opinion
senses.definition: holding views that avoid the extremes of left and right, or of any strong division
senses.definitionCN: 持避免左右极端或任何强烈对立的观点
senses.example: The paper speaks to middle voters who dislike both extremes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸面向不喜欢两个极端的中间选民。
senses.why: A political spectrum is imagined as a line with two ends, so the party or voter near its centre is called middle; the spatial image is simply carried into public life.
senses.whyCN: 政治光谱被想象成一条有两个端点的线，靠近中心位置的党派或选民就被称为 middle；空间的形象就这样搬进了公共生活。

intro.en: Middle is the full form of the old root that also gives the short word mid; its history runs from a prehistoric root, through Old English, into everyday modern senses such as waist and moderate politics.
intro.cn: middle 是古老词根的完整形式，短词 mid 也出自同一来源；它的历史从史前词根出发，经古英语，一直走到今天「腰部」与「温和政治」这类日常义项。

items.en: The reconstructed root *medhyo- meant middle and is the common ancestor of English middle and Latin medius.
items.cn: 重构词根 *medhyo- 意为「中间」，是英语 middle 与拉丁语 medius 的共同祖先。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as *midilaz or *medilaz, a noun and adjective for the central part of something.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中的形式一般重构为 *midilaz 或 *medilaz，是表示某物中部的名词与形容词。

items.en: Old English middel added the suffix -el to the root, giving a full adjective and noun beside the shorter midd.
items.cn: 古英语 middel 在词根后加后缀 -el，在较短的 midd 之外提供了一个完整的形容词与名词。

items.en: Middle English kept middel and middle side by side, and the noun already covered space, time and the human waist.
items.cn: 中古英语中 middel 与 middle 并行使用，名词已经同时覆盖空间、时间与人的腰部。

items.en: Modern English settled on middle, extended it to social and political moderation, and kept it in fixed phrases such as middle class and middle age.
items.cn: 现代英语最终确定拼写为 middle，把词义扩展到社会与政治的温和立场，并保留在 middle class、middle age 这类固定说法中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin middle root or merely close in spelling; the near-meaning group collects other words for the centre.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「中间」词根上的词，或仅仅拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示中心的词。

entries.definition: To interfere in something that is not one's business; it is unrelated to middle and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 干涉与自己无关的事；它与 middle 没有词源关系，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Situated in the middle, especially in anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 位于中间的，尤用于解剖学。

entries.definition: The middle value in an ordered set, or a line through the middle.
entries.definitionCN: 有序数值中的中间值，或经过中点的线。

entries.definition: Something in the middle, such as a middle size or a means of communication.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间的事物，如中号尺寸或传播媒介。

entries.definition: The exact middle point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的正中心点。

entries.definition: The exact middle point of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的正中心点。

entries.definition: The central and most important part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物最中心、最重要的部分。

entries.definition: A point exactly halfway between two ends.
entries.definitionCN: 正好位于两端中间的点。

normalIntro.en: Middle is the long form of the old middle root, and its family keeps returning to the idea of a point that divides a whole into equal parts.
normalIntro.cn: middle 是古老「中间」词根的完整形式，它的一族词反复回到同一个想法：把整体分成相等两部分的那一点。

normal.en: Middle is the full form beside the short mid, the way middle school is longer than midterm.
normal.cn: middle 是短词 mid 的完整形式，就像 middle school 比 midterm 更长一样。

normal.en: Old English added -el to the root, a suffix that also appears in words for small tools, so middle is a built form rather than a bare root.
normal.cn: 古英语在词根后加了 -el，这个后缀也出现在表示小工具的词汇里，所以 middle 是构造出来的形式，而不是光秃秃的词根。

normal.en: Latin medius is a genuine cousin, which links middle to medial, median and medium.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 是真正的同族词，把 middle 与 medial、median、medium 连在一起。

normal.en: The phrases middle class and middle age show how easily the spatial word moves into social life.
normal.cn: middle class 与 middle age 展示了这个空间词多么容易走进社会生活。

normal.en: In the middle of is the everyday frame: whatever follows it is the thing being cut into two halves.
normal.cn: in the middle of 是日常框架：后面接的东西，就是被分成两半的那件事。

abstract.en: A vase placed at the exact centre of a long table turns the table into two equal halves.
abstract.cn: 花瓶摆在长桌的正中央，桌子就被分成了两个相等的半边。

abstract.en: Middle is a balancing word: it keeps both ends at the same distance and refuses to choose.
abstract.cn: middle 是个平衡词：它让两端保持同等距离，拒绝偏向任何一边。

abstract.en: From a row of seats to a political debate, the same centre keeps being found and named.
abstract.cn: 从一排座位到一场政治辩论，同一个中心不断被找到、被命名。

examples.en: There is a fountain in the middle of the square.
examples.cn: 广场中央有一座喷泉。

examples.en: The project ran into trouble in the middle of the summer.
examples.cn: 这个项目在夏季中期遇到了麻烦。

examples.en: Put the tallest child in the middle row.
examples.cn: 把最高的孩子安排在中间那一排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米的」——长桌正中的花瓶离两边一样远，米尺量到一半就叫 middle。

root: 古英语 middel，由表示「中间」的词根加后缀 -el 构成，更早来自原始日耳曼语 *midilaz；拉丁语 medius（中间的）为同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the point equally far from both ends; the senses carry that point into space, time, the body, a rank, and the moderate centre of politics.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是距离两端同样远的那一点；各义项把这个点带进空间、时间、身体、名次，以及政治上的温和中间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vase at the exact centre of a long table, with chairs arranged evenly on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌正中央摆着一只花瓶，两侧椅子均匀排开。

branches.en: a fountain standing where the paths cross
branches.cn: 立在道路交会处的喷泉

branches.en: a project stalling halfway through summer
branches.cn: 在夏季过半时停滞的工程

branches.en: a rope tied around a narrow waist
branches.cn: 系在窄腰上的绳子

branches.en: a child seated between the front and back rows
branches.cn: 坐在前排与后排之间的孩子

branches.en: a voter standing between two shouting camps
branches.cn: 夹在两个高声阵营之间的选民

intro.cn: middle 是词根加一个古老后缀，而同一个拉丁词根 medius 提供了整批表示中心与中间的词。

definition_zh: 感觉；意义；理智；感觉到
definition_en: a feeling from the body, the meaning of something, good judgment, or to become aware of something
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到杯壁，热度顺着皮肤传上来
scene: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。 She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 sensed 是「感觉到」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

derivatives.zh: 明智的
敏感的
感觉；轰动
感官的
无意义的；失去知觉的

senses.title: Body feeling
senses.definition: a feeling produced by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 由感官产生的感觉
senses.example: She felt a sense of warmth from the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 她从杯子上感到一阵暖意。
senses.why: This is the basic sensory sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的感官义。

senses.title: Meaning
senses.definition: the meaning that words or actions carry
senses.definitionCN: 词语或行为所承载的意义
senses.example: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。
senses.why: Meaning is what the mind grasps.
senses.whyCN: 意义是心智所把握的东西。

senses.title: Good judgment
senses.definition: practical good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 实际而良好的判断力
senses.example: It is common sense to lock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 锁门是常识。
senses.why: The mind's sense becomes sound judgment.
senses.whyCN: 心智的感觉变成健全的判断。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become aware of something without being told
senses.definitionCN: 未经告知而察觉到某事
senses.example: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of perceiving.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为感知的动作。

intro.en: Sense comes from Latin sentire, to feel, through Latin sensus, a feeling.
intro.cn: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），经拉丁语 sensus（感觉）而来。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或察觉。

items.en: Sensus named a feeling or meaning.
items.cn: sensus 指感觉或意义。

items.en: Sens carried both feeling and meaning.
items.cn: sens 兼具感觉与意义。

items.en: Sense added the idea of good judgment.
items.cn: sense 增加了良好判断之义。

items.en: Make sense became a common phrase.
items.cn: make sense 成为常用短语。

note.en: Sense is compared with similar-looking words and with words for feeling and meaning.
note.cn: 把 sense 与形近词以及表示感觉和意义的词作比较。

entries.definition: from a past time until now

entries.definition: a smell

entries.definition: plural of sense

entries.definition: an emotional or physical state
entries.definitionCN: 感觉

normalIntro.en: Sense covers what the body feels, what words mean, and what the mind judges.
normalIntro.cn: sense 涵盖身体所感、词语所表与心智所判。

normal.en: We have five senses.
normal.cn: 我们有五种感官。

normal.en: A sentence must make sense.
normal.cn: 一个句子必须讲得通。

normal.en: Common sense is judgment without special training.
normal.cn: 常识是无需专门训练的判断力。

normal.en: She sensed danger before she saw it.
normal.cn: 她在看见危险之前就察觉到了。

normal.en: In a sense, both answers are right.
normal.cn: 在某种意义上，两个答案都对。

abstract.en: Meaning is the shape a feeling takes when it is shared.
abstract.cn: 意义是感觉被分享时呈现的形状。

abstract.en: Good judgment is feeling trained by experience.
abstract.cn: 良好的判断力是被经验训练过的感觉。

abstract.en: We notice most what we have learned to sense.
abstract.cn: 我们最容易察觉自己学会去感受的东西。

examples.en: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
examples.cn: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

examples.en: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
examples.cn: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。

examples.en: It is common sense to lock the door.
examples.cn: 锁门是常识。

dict_mnemonic.text: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），本义「感官所感」，后扩展为意义、判断力与察觉。

root: 源自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），核心义「感知与领会」。

sensesIntro.en: Sense means a body feeling, a meaning, good judgment, or the act of perceiving.
sensesIntro.cn: sense 意为身体感觉、意义、理智或察觉。

core.en: The mind and body taking in what is there.
core.cn: 身心对眼前之物的接收。

branches.en: Warmth, smell, or sound received by the body.
branches.cn: 身体接收到的热、气味或声音。

branches.en: What a sentence or action means.
branches.cn: 句子或行为所表达的意思。

branches.en: Practical judgment about daily life.
branches.cn: 关于日常生活的实际判断。

branches.en: Noticing something before being told.
branches.cn: 在被告知之前就注意到某事。

branches.en: Feeling and noticing are two sides of one act.
branches.cn: 感受与察觉是同一动作的两面。

intro.en: Sense belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling and perceiving.
intro.cn: sense 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire and sensus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 与 sensus 是历史词根。

items.example: He has a sense of duty.

items.exampleCN: 这个设备正在感应运动。

items.example: The cold caused a burning sensation.

definition_zh: 憎恨；讨厌；怨恨；仇恨
definition_en: to feel very strong dislike for someone or something
core_image: 背过身去推开碗：连看都不想看一眼的强烈排斥
scene: 弟弟最讨厌吃芹菜，一闻到那股味道就把碗推得远远的。 He hates celery so much that he pushes the bowl away at once.
sceneCN: 这里 hate 是「讨厌、厌恶」（第 1 个义项：强烈不喜欢）；弟弟一闻到味道就推开碗，正是 hate 表示强烈反感的日常用法。

derivatives.zh: 憎恨；仇恨，由 hate 加名词后缀构成的强义名词
可恶的；充满仇恨的，由 hate 加后缀 -ful 构成
怀恨者；反对者，由 hate 加施动者后缀 -er 构成

senses.title: To dislike strongly
senses.definition: to feel a very strong dislike for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事感到强烈的不喜欢
senses.example: I hate getting up early on cold mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 我讨厌在寒冷的早晨早起。
senses.why: The core image is pushing a bowl away: the body turns from the object, so hate names the strongest form of dislike.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是推开碗：身体背对对象，hate 因此表示不喜欢情绪的最强形式。

senses.title: To feel intense hostility
senses.definition: to feel extreme anger and hostility toward a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体感到极端的愤怒与敌意
senses.example: He hated the men who had destroyed his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他憎恨那些毁掉他家庭的人。
senses.why: When dislike is fed by pain and memory, it hardens into hostility, and hate becomes a settled emotion rather than a passing mood.
senses.whyCN: 当反感被痛苦和记忆喂养，它就硬化成敌意，hate 由一时情绪变成持久的情感状态。

senses.title: To regret or be sorry
senses.definition: used to say politely that you are sorry to do something
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表示不愿做某事
senses.example: I hate to trouble you, but could you help me?
senses.exampleCN: 我很不愿打扰你，但能帮个忙吗？

intro.en: Hate runs through Germanic languages as the word for strong dislike.
intro.cn: hate 贯穿各日耳曼语言，是表示强烈厌恶的词。

items.en: Old English had the verb hatian, meaning to hate or hold as an enemy.

items.en: It comes from a Germanic root *hataz, the standard word for hostility in the family.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hataz，是日耳曼语族中表示敌意的标准词。

items.en: Old Norse hata reinforced the English verb after Viking settlements.
items.cn: 维京人定居后，古诺斯语 hata 强化了英语的这个动词。

items.en: In Middle English, hate appeared widely as both verb and noun in songs and chronicles.
items.cn: 中古英语中，hate 以动词与名词两种身份广泛出现在诗歌与编年史里。

items.en: Modern English added compounds like hate speech and hate crime for hostility turned into action.
items.cn: 现代英语新增 hate speech、hate crime 等复合词，描述化为行动的敌意。

note.cn: hate 的形近词与厌恶义场的近邻。

scene: 跑道上，一名选手跑在队伍的最前面。 The team is ahead by two points.

senses.title: In front
senses.definition: in a position in front of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在某人或某物前面的位置
senses.example: The road ahead was clear.
senses.exampleCN: 前面的路很通畅。
senses.why: Ahead is a plus head, and the head is at the front, so the word pictures being at the front of a line.
senses.whyCN: ahead 由 a 与 head 构成，头所在的位置就是队伍的前面。

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: before the expected time
senses.definitionCN: 在预定的时间之前
senses.example: We arrived ahead of the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在人群之前到达。
senses.why: Being in front was applied to time, where it means earlier than expected.
senses.whyCN: 把「在前面」用到时间上，就是比预期更早。

senses.title: Leading in a contest
senses.definition: in front in a race or a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或竞争中处在前面
senses.example: The team is ahead by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍领先两分。
senses.why: In a race, the one in front is the one leading.
senses.whyCN: 在比赛中处在前面，就是领先。

senses.title: Forward
senses.definition: onward in the direction one faces
senses.definitionCN: 朝面对的方向继续
senses.example: Move ahead slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢向前移动。
senses.why: Moving in the direction the head faces is moving forward.
senses.whyCN: 朝头所对的方向走，就是向前。

items.en: Sailors used ahead for the front of a ship.
items.cn: 水手用 ahead 指船的前方。

items.en: The word came to mean earlier in time as well.

items.en: Today it covers place, time and progress.

definition_zh: 主人；硕士；大师；能手；精通；掌握；控制；制服
definition_en: a person who owns or has authority over something, an advanced university degree, an expert in a craft, or to learn and gain complete control of something
core_image: 老人一抬手，院子里的人和马都停下来等他的吩咐
scene: 旧宅的院子里，一位老人牵马走到廊下，抬手示意年轻仆人不必再跟着。 The old master of the house knew every corner of the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 master 是「主人」（第 1 个义项：对一处宅院、牲畜或仆役拥有支配权的人）；句意为这座宅子的老主人熟悉园子的每一个角落。图中可辨识物件：廊下的马、抬手示意的老人、退后的仆人。

derivatives.zh: 由 master 加表示「状态、性质」的后缀 -y 构成，义为「精通；掌控」
由 master 加表示「充满……」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「有掌控力的；技艺高超的」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，本指学徒期满后用以证明手艺的作品，义为「杰作」
由 master 加 -ly 构成，义为「精巧的；显出大师手笔的」

senses.title: The owner or head of a household
senses.definition: a person who owns a house, an animal or a servant and has authority over them
senses.definitionCN: 对一处宅院、一头牲畜或一名仆役拥有所有权并有权支配的人
senses.example: The dog follows its master everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这条狗到处跟着它的主人。
senses.why: Latin magister named the man who stood above others, and the first English uses kept that household power: the master is the one whose word is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magister 指站在他人之上的人，英语最早的用法保留的正是这种宅院里的权力：主人就是话被听从的那一位。

senses.title: A holder of a master's degree
senses.definition: an advanced university degree below a doctorate, or the person who holds it
senses.definitionCN: 低于博士学位的大学高级学位，也指持有这一学位的人
senses.example: She took a master's degree in urban planning.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了城市规划专业的硕士学位。
senses.why: In the medieval university the magister was the licensed teacher, so the title of the qualified teacher became the name of the highest taught degree.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的大学里，magister 是取得授课资格的老师，于是「合格教师」这个头衔后来成了最高的授课型学位之名。

senses.title: An expert in a craft or art
senses.definition: a person who is highly skilled in a craft, an art or a technique
senses.definitionCN: 在某门手艺、艺术或技艺上极为精湛的人
senses.example: The glass master shaped the bowl with three quick turns.
senses.exampleCN: 那位玻璃大师转了三下就把碗形定了下来。
senses.why: Because magister marked the person who had finished the whole training, skill itself came to be measured by the word: a master is the one at the top of the craft.
senses.whyCN: 因为 magister 标出的是完成了全部训练的人，技艺高低便用这个词来衡量：大师就是一门手艺里站在顶端的那一个。

senses.title: To learn or understand something completely
senses.definition: to learn a skill or subject so well that you can use it without effort
senses.definitionCN: 把一项技能或一门学问学到运用自如的程度
senses.example: He mastered the old engine by taking it apart twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那台旧发动机拆了两遍，就把它摸透了。
senses.why: The noun for a qualified teacher turned into a verb: to master a thing is to reach the level at which you could explain it to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 指「合格老师」的名词转成了动词：master 一样东西，就是达到能够把它讲给别人听的水平。

senses.title: To bring something under control
senses.definition: to gain control over a strong feeling, an animal or a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 把强烈的情绪、一头动物或困难的局面压住并置于掌控之下
senses.example: She mastered her anger before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把怒气压住，才开口回答。
senses.why: If a master is the person who gives orders, the verb can also mean making a wild thing obey, and the object shifts from a skill to whatever refuses to be controlled.
senses.whyCN: 既然 master 是发号施令的人，动词也就表示让不听话的东西服从，宾语于是从一门技能转到任何不肯受控的对象。

intro.en: Master comes from Latin magister, the man with authority, and reached English through Old French; the word still carries both the power to command and the title of a qualified teacher.
intro.cn: master 出自拉丁语 magister（有权威的人），经古法语进入英语；这个词至今同时带着发号施令的权力与「合格教师」的头衔。

items.en: Magis is the Latin adverb for more or rather, and it marks the greater side of any comparison.
items.cn: magis 是拉丁语副词，意为「更多、更」，标出任何比较中更强的那一边。

items.en: Magister was built on magis with a comparative ending and named the man placed above others, above all the teacher in charge of pupils.
items.cn: magister 由 magis 加比较级词尾构成，指被置于他人之上的人，首先指管教学生的老师。

items.en: Old French kept the word as maistre, a lord, teacher or craftsman, and its spelling travelled into English with the Norman court.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 maistre，指领主、教师或匠人，它的拼写随诺曼宫廷传入英语。

items.en: Middle English master covered the head of a house, the qualified teacher and the skilled craftsman, and the universities gave it to a degree.
items.cn: 中古英语的 master 兼指一家之主、合格教师与熟练匠人，大学又把这个称号给了一个学位。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb to master, keeps the academic degree, and still uses the noun for an animal's owner and for a supreme practitioner.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词 master，保留了学位义，也仍用这个名词指动物的主人与某一行的顶尖高手。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and Latin relatives of the word; the near group gathers names for owners, experts and the highly skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的派生词与拉丁同族词；近义组收表示主人、专家与高超技艺者的词。

entries.definition: Showing great skill or firm control.

entries.definition: A performer with outstanding technical skill.
